audit.whatIsWrong: The chart read Aurora/Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill/Ryze/Ryze in both layers while the whys underneath describe a completely different lane: whys[0] has Ryze ahead at 1, whys[2] has Aurora winning 3, whys[3] has Ryze taking the 4-5 grind, whys[4] has Aurora owning 6.
audit.why: The packet levelChart (Ryze/Skill/Aurora/Ryze/Aurora/Ryze/Ryze) matches the prose exactly. The mirror (aurora__ryze) spotted the same disagreement and deliberately left it for a decision rather than resolving it.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 2, 3 and 4 set to Ryze/Aurora/Ryze/Aurora in both layers as matched pairs, ratings moved with them, and the two templated phase whys that then argued the wrong side rewritten.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[2] calls her ultimate "Between the Worlds" and claims it interrupts a Realm Warp "channel" and that her "W exile" removes the anchor point.
audit.why: The ability is Between Worlds: a 250-range leap releasing a shockwave that damages and slows, leaving an area that slows enemies and lets Aurora teleport from one side of it to the other. There is no exile and no displacement in her kit. Realm Warp is not a channel either — it creates a portal that fires after a delay, so the real threat is that her zone sits on the ground the portal needs.
audit.corrected: Correct name, the real leap range and slow-field mechanic, and the honest reason the level-6 window is hers.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer attributes her leap-and-stealth to E throughout ("E blink", "E hop", "E-blink engage") and repeatedly credits her with a root off Q.
audit.why: Across the Veil is W (700 range, 22/21/20/19/18): she leaps, lands invisible in the spirit realm, and gains Move Speed — that is the ability that leaves Rune Prison. The Weirding is E (825, 15/14/13/12/11): a blast that damages and slows, then hops her backward. Twofold Hex is Q (900, 9/8.5/8/7.5/7): a curse missile she recasts to drag the curses back. Riot's text gives Q no crowd control at all, so the 'Q root burst' the page builds its level-3 advice on is not in the kit.
audit.corrected: Every leap reference renamed to Across the Veil with its 22s rank-1 cooldown as the actual trade window, The Weirding named for the slow, and the fabricated Q root removed rather than replaced with a guess.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing on the page mentions Grievous Wounds despite Spirit Abjuration healing her off every spell and attack that damages you.
audit.why: Her passive exorcises spirits from damaged enemies which then follow her and heal — in an extended lane of chip trades that healing is what decides the exchange.
audit.corrected: Anti-heal added to the itemization block and the healing named as the reason chip alone does not close her out.

edits.before: At level 1 you have a narrow head start — Q her before she sets up her poke rhythm, but do not walk into her auto-attack range to Flux-stack; she has no blink yet and cannot dodge your Overload. The moment she hits level 2 and gains her E hop, that window closes hard. Level 3 is her spike, not yours: her E-blink closes the gap, her root sets up burst, and her passive spirit stacks amplify everything. Play behind the minion wave, accept that she wins the contested trade, and farm with Q at its maximum cast range — your W root is useless if she blinks out of it the instant it lands.
edits.after: At level 1 you have a narrow head start — Overload reaches 1000 against her 900 Twofold Hex, so poke on its flat 5s cooldown and never walk the 615 in for Spell Flux. Once Across the Veil (W) comes up she can leap 700 units and land invisible, and that window closes hard. Level 3 is her spike, not yours: the leap opens or ends any trade she likes, The Weirding slows you as she hops away, and her spirits heal back the chip. Play behind the wave, accept that she wins the contested trade, and farm at maximum Q range — your root is worthless if she leaves the instant it lands.

edits.before: Levels 4 and 5 swing back to you because her E-blink has a real cooldown and she cannot poke freely without it — when it is down, walk up and drop E on her, cycling W-root into empowered Q while she has no escape. At 6 that math reverses again: Between the Worlds lets her zone the entire frontline and punishes any Realm Warp channel you attempt by exiling you mid-ult. Never channel Realm Warp near her unless she has already burned her W; treat her level-6 zone as a hard stop on your macro pressure until you can bait it out.
edits.after: Levels 4 and 5 swing back to you because Across the Veil costs her 22 seconds at rank 1 and she cannot step up safely without it — in that gap, walk up, Spell Flux her, and cycle W-root into Q while she has no way out. At 6 the math reverses: Between Worlds lays a slow field she teleports across, and Realm Warp is a portal that fires after a delay, so it is standing terrain she gets to zone. Never place the portal near her unless the leap is already spent; treat her 6 as a stop on your macro until you bait it.

edits.before: Once Seraph's Embrace completes, your combo is near-permanently available and your Flux cascade out-damages her sustained poke in a straight exchange — she needs to blink in to engage on you and that blink is also her only escape from your W root, so a well-timed root wins the trade. At 2+ items your CDR is deep enough that you can E-Q-W-Q again before her blink resets, making isolated fights heavily Ryze-favored; she must group with her team to stay safe, which is exactly where your Realm Warp becomes the game-deciding tool rather than a lane mechanic.
edits.after: Once Seraph's Embrace completes, your combo is near-permanently available and your Flux cascade out-damages her poke in a straight exchange — Across the Veil is both her engage and her only exit from Rune Prison, so a root timed after the leap wins the trade outright. At 2+ items your cooldowns cycle E-Q-W-Q again well before her 18-second leap returns, making isolated fights heavily Ryze-favoured; she must group to stay safe, which is exactly where Realm Warp stops being a lane mechanic and decides games.

notes: Two systemic errors on this page, both likely template-wide. First, the content layer put Aurora's leap-and-stealth on E; it is Across the Veil (W), and E is The Weirding. Second, the page repeatedly credits Aurora with a root off Q — Riot's text for Twofold Hex gives it no crowd control, so I removed the claim rather than substituting a guess. I also removed the assertion that Between Worlds 'exiles' Ryze mid-ultimate: nothing in her kit displaces or exiles, and Realm Warp is a delayed portal rather than a channel. Chart flipped to the packet ordering, which the page's own whys already argued; the mirror saw the same disagreement and left it flagged rather than resolving it, so if aurora__ryze is re-run it should be flipped to match.
